purpose: Levobunolol is an eye drop used to lower pressure inside your eye. It is commonly prescribed for glaucoma or a condition called ocular hypertension. Keeping that eye pressure under control helps protect your vision over time.
how_it_works: Your eye constantly makes a fluid that can build up and raise pressure if it does not drain well. Levobunolol works by reducing the amount of that fluid your eye produces. This lowers the pressure and helps prevent damage to your optic nerve.
common_side_effects: Temporary stinging or burning right after putting in the drops, mild eye redness or itching, blurred vision right after use, and occasionally a slower heart rate or feeling tired since a small amount can be absorbed into your body.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have asthma, COPD, a slow heart rate, heart failure, or diabetes, because the medicine absorbed through your eye can sometimes affect these conditions. Do not stop using the drops suddenly without talking to your doctor. If you wear soft contact lenses, remove them before putting in the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. Tell your doctor about all other eye drops or medicines you take.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 1 drop in the affected eye once or twice a day, depending on what your doctor prescribes. Try to use it at the same time each day. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between them.
